clue.text: Traditional dinner in pan

definitions.meaning: the Sunday joint of meat cooked in the oven, a British tradition
to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does

explanation.surface: A cook prepares the customary meal in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a roast is the classic Sunday meal, and to roast a play is to savage it in a review.

clue.text: Bailiff's task in hearing to support preaching lord who needs a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other
in a down clue a lift raises the letters, reading them upwards

parts.note: Lord Soper was a famous Methodist preacher in London
a session is a sitting or hearing of a court

explanation.surface: A bailiff at a court hearing supports an evangelist peer.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Soper, Lord Soper, preached at Speakers' Corner. SOPER lifted gives REPOS, with SESSION below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bailiffs seize goods from debtors, the act of taking property back.

clue.text: Support for drying land voiced

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, a land

explanation.surface: A clothes rack for drying is described aloud as land.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire, the Irish name for Ireland, is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse or rack used for drying laundry.

clue.text: Don't start to feed fuel to maintain worst assembled type of engine

indicators.note: to maintain means to hold, so the letters sit inside
Don't start means the first letter is not used

parts.note: to stoke is to feed fuel to a fire

indicators.note: assembled means put together in a new way

explanation.surface: A mechanic is told not to begin refuelling a badly built engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' trims the synonym; 'assembled' turns WORST into WOSTR, which goes in after the first letter. 'type' is a kind of engine, not printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-stroke engine completes its power cycle in two piston strokes, a common engine design.

clue.text: Two fashions: each comes in, only to peter out

indicators.note: comes in says the next piece enters between the other letters

parts.note: a fad and a way are both fashions or modes
way, as in a way of doing things, is a fashion

explanation.surface: Fashion trends arrive only to fizzle out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two fashions' supplies two different words, not the same one twice; 'only to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade away and to peter out both mean to dwindle gradually to nothing.

clue.text: Loud insect circles tree

indicators.note: circles means goes round another piece

parts.note: a fly is an insect
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A noisy bug flies round a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud in the sense of gaudy or showy clothing matches flashy.

clue.text: Becoming absorbent, cap removed after month

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word behind the month

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December

indicators.note: cap removed means the top letter is taken off

parts.note: porous means absorbent

explanation.surface: An absorbent hat without its top worn after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming in the sense of seemly or proper is a synonym for decorous behaviour.

clue.text: Grant one's immature, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: callow means young and inexperienced

explanation.surface: A youngster named Grant is inexperienced and loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is a link; Grant is a verb, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to permit it.

clue.text: A stream drowns rabid old mammal

indicators.note: drowns means covers over, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a rill is a small stream
rabid means mad

explanation.surface: A small river drowns a frenzied ancient animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured animal of the Americas is a mammal.

clue.text: No romances pull off the promise of romance

indicators.note: off, as in gone off or wrong, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Love affairs that fail to attract contrast with the hope that a newspaper ad can offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges NO ROMANCES PULL. 'Pull' looks like the verb of the surface but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely-hearts advertisements appeared in the newspaper section of private messages, so it held out hope of romance.

clue.text: Riot about securing bathroom product

indicators.note: about means placed around another piece

parts.note: a riot is a scream, something hilarious
having means obtaining or securing

explanation.surface: Disorder breaks out over the purchase of toiletries.
explanation.walkthrough: A riot is used in the sense of a very funny thing, also called a scream.
explanation.definitionFit: A foam applied before using a razor is a bathroom toiletry.

clue.text: Makeshift bed for one yawning?

definitions.meaning: a portable frame for carrying a casualty or a spare bed
someone yawning often stretches the arms, so is one who stretches

explanation.surface: A tired person on a temporary cot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: a person yawning stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a canvas frame used as an improvised bed, and literally one who stretches.

clue.text: Land's End ringed by using compass

indicators.note: ringed by says the piece is surrounded by another

parts.note: with means using, as in cut with a knife

indicators.note: End points to the final letter of the word land

explanation.surface: A navigator finds the far tip of Cornwall by using a compass.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End, the far southwest tip of Cornwall, splits: its last letter D goes inside WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of range or extent is a synonym for breadth.

clue.text: One merry as king about to capture knight and bishop together

indicators.note: to capture says the next letters are held inside
about tells us to turn the name round

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme was a merry old soul
N is the chess notation for knight
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A jolly monarch takes two chessmen at once.
explanation.walkthrough: COLE turned 'about' gives ELOC, which captures N and B after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English to mean all at once, as a single group.

clue.text: Australian native to speak tenderly in villain's embrace

indicators.note: in, with embrace, says one piece sits inside
an embrace holds the cooing within the villain

parts.note: a bandit is a villain
to coo is to speak softly and lovingly

explanation.surface: An Aussie whispers sweet nothings in a crook's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: This small marsupial is native to Australia.

clue.text: Former European capital almost gaining a sign of victory after bloke retreats

indicators.note: after puts the remaining pieces behind the reversed bloke
retreats means the word goes backwards

parts.note: guy is a synonym for bloke

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway
V for victory, Churchill's two-finger sign

explanation.surface: A man retreats while a capital city nearly celebrates a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former European' is a citizen of a country that broke up in the 1990s; 'gaining' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former Yugoslavia, a country that no longer exists, is a former European nationality.

clue.text: Mobile art seldom great work

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Moving art is rarely a masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting by a great European artist of earlier centuries is a great work.

clue.text: Politician in small way superior to Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue superior means placed above

parts.note: mini means small
St is street, a way
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A politician who is little and regards himself as above the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister is a politician holding office.

clue.text: Type of fairness that's crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A kind of justice that turns out to be corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges FAIRNESS; 'Type' is printing type, not a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface without serifs is a category of printing type.

clue.text: Neighbour Jack in trouble at home

indicators.note: in says Jack goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
J is the card abbreviation for jack
in means at home

explanation.surface: A neighbour called Jack is having problems at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' is a verb here, meaning to border on.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something is to lie next to it or border it.

clue.text: Noon at 11.59 am? Almost

parts.note: a minute before noon is early in relation to noon

explanation.surface: A minute before midday is close to noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost both mean not quite.

clue.text: Opening in college

definitions.meaning: a projecting bay window, an opening in a wall
one of the colleges of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A window set in a college wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window, and Oriel is a college of Oxford University.

clue.text: Pick up runs in poor situation

indicators.note: in means runs goes inside the other word

parts.note: a lean time is a poor situation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A team scores runs in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill is to learn it.

clue.text: Appearing upset, since tail's stiff

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An animal looks upset because its tail has gone rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SINCE TAIL; the 's of tail's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unable to stretch or give is stiff, lacking elasticity.

clue.text: Beginning to tie red or white string

indicators.note: Beginning to means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: wine is red or white

explanation.surface: Starting to tie red or white thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: twine is a strong cord made of twisted strands, a kind of string used for tying parcels.

clue.text: Mark of boy racer, in poor visibility turning Daisy's stomach

indicators.note: turning means the word is reversed

parts.note: fog causes poor visibility
an aster is a daisy-like flower, plus the S of the possessive
tripe is the stomach lining of cattle used as food

explanation.surface: A reckless young driver in fog makes a girl called Daisy feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: FOG reversed by 'turning' gives GOF. Daisy is a flower, not a girl. A boy racer is a British term for a young man who drives fast and flashily.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted stripe along a car's side is the stereotypical decoration of a young show-off driver.

clue.text: Venomous creature tight round tailless rodent

indicators.note: round says the mean word encloses the next piece

parts.note: tight means mean with money, stingy

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal wraps itself around a rat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' here means mean with money, not taut or drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat sea fish has a venomous barb on its tail.

clue.text: Discharge man in grip of drink

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside the other word

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
he is a male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: A man in the clutches of alcohol has a runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucus discharge from the eyes or nose.
